notes: JADS is a multilateral capacity-building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan with no single attached institution. The official AfDB page (afdb.org, last updated 11-Sep-2024) states scholars 'pursue post-graduate studies at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, and engineering' and the linked 'List of Universities' page distributes awards across multiple Japanese host universities (University of Tokyo, Sophia University, Kyoto University, Hiroshima University, Kogakuin University, Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University), with further African hosts (UNZA, E-JUST) still under negotiation. Only programme administrators are named (JADS Secretariat: Keiko Takei, Moumine Sissao, Ely Shabani Katembo, Antoine T. Akaffou, Hendrina C. Doroba) - these are AfDB programme task managers, not supervising professors, and their emails are Cloudflare-obfuscated on the page. Host-university admissions offices are listed as contacts, not academic supervisors. No professor tie is published, so no professor entries are recorded.

U.S. Department of State exchange programme (Young African Leaders Initiative) administered by IREX; a six-week non-degree executive-style institute hosted at many different U.S. colleges and universities each year plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience, with no single named academic supervisor. The official apply page (mandelawashingtonfellowship.org/apply, checked live) lists only a general programme contact, mwfellowship@irex.org, which is an administrative address rather than an institutional professor email. Host institutes vary per cohort, so no supervising professor is published anywhere in the official material.

notes: Evidence chain (all on aims.ac.za, the official institute domain): scholarship page https://aims.ac.za/academics/prospective_students (Structured Master's scholarship: tuition and research fees, flights, accommodation, R2,200/month stipend; January intake for South African applicants) -> Structured Master's page https://aims.ac.za/academics/msc/ ('one-year postgraduate programme... accredited by the Universities of Cape Town, Stellenbosch University, and the University of the Western Cape'; semester 3 = 'a three-month long research project' where 'students work on a research topic with a supervisor') -> Research Centre faculty listing https://aims.ac.za/research-centre/ under 'Our Researchers'. Individual researcher profile pages publish no email addresses; the only published address on aims.ac.za is the generic info@aims.ac.za (https://aims.ac.za/contact/) and contribute@aims.ac.za for project proposals, so official_email is null and official_email_verified is false for every entry - no address was constructed or guessed. Discipline tags (research_areas) are taken from the AIMS Research Centre 'Our Researchers' listing. AIMS's management team page (https://aims.ac.za/team/) also lists Karin-Therese Howell as Executive Director, Jacques Rabie as Mathematical Innovation Manager and Acting Academic Director, and Ulrich Paquet as AI Director. Other resident researchers exist (e.g. Prof. Amanda Weltman, cosmology, whose profile states her primary affiliation is the University of Cape Town) but the maximum of three entries was applied, prioritising the academic leadership and on-site research faculty of the funded programme.

UNHCR-run tertiary refugee scholarship programme (DAFI); no attached institution. The official programme page (scholarshipsplatform.com DAFI Programme Management Platform) is JavaScript-only and required headless-browser rendering to read, but it confirms there is no host institution: "UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) offers qualified refugee and returnee (in selected countries*) students the possibility to earn an undergraduate degree in their country of asylum or home country" and "DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies." Applications are handled by individual UNHCR country operations and partners (e.g. afgka@unhcr.org, kenya@unhcr.org with dafiapplicationskenya@windle.org, dafi@sda-lb.org) via a per-country contact list - these are programme offices, not supervising professors. Because scholars enrol at whatever institution they have access to in their country of asylum or home country, no supervising professor is published anywhere in the official material.

The University of Westminster Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarship (checked live at westminster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships/postgraduate-sanctuary-scholarship) is a university-wide award: two scholarships covering 'Full tuition fee waiver and £1000/month for up to 12 months' for any eligible full-time master's course starting January 2027, with eligibility limited only by immigration status and exclusion of PG Dip, professional, conversion and integrated MPhil courses. No programme, department or academic is named, and the page names no professor or supervisor; the single published contact is the central Scholarships Team address scholarships@westminster.ac.uk, which is an administrative mailbox rather than an institutional professor email. No supervisor tie can be evidenced from the official page, so no professor entries were invented.

The University of Glasgow Sanctuary Scholarship (checked live at gla.ac.uk/scholarships/sanctuaryscholarships) is an institution-wide award for applicants with refugee/asylum-seeker status holding an offer for 2027/28 entry, open to 'prospective undergraduate and postgraduate taught students' across roughly 200 listed eligible programmes (AI in Education, Advanced Mathematics, Climate & Environmental Science, Robotics & AI, TESOL, etc.), providing a full tuition fee waiver plus a GBP 4,000/5,000 per year stipend. No professor, department or research group is named on the official scholarship page and no supervisor is attached to the award; enquiries are directed to the Scholarships Team via the enquiry form (https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/contact/) rather than to any named academic. Because the scholarship is not tied to a specific programme or supervisor, no professor entries could be evidenced.

The Ernst Mach Grant - worldwide is a national mobility grant of the Republic of Austria implemented by OeAD-GmbH on behalf of the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research. The official OeAD programme listing (oead.at/en/the-oead/our-programmes-from-a-to-z) states it 'is intended for young researchers and university lecturers of all disciplines who are studying or pursuing research outside Austria and want to do a research project in Austria' (target group: postgraduates, postdocs; countries of origin: all; duration 1-9 months; closing date 1 December) - applicants themselves choose and arrange any Austrian host institution and host professor, so no supervising professor is attached to the scheme. The named contacts in the listing are OeAD programme officers (e.g. Sigrid Koller, Head of Sector Academic Mobility; Katharina Engel, Coordinator Mobility) rather than supervising professors. The supplied official_source_url (grants.at encoded deep link) resolves only to the generic grants.at landing page; the Ernst Mach Grant worldwide entry was verified through the OeAD A-Z programme page linked from it, and the database itself (grants.at/what-is-grantsat) describes itself as a directory in which applicants 'apply directly to the authority' with no attached supervisor.
